text:
Maria: Heads up — noticed a weird spike in canary fallback for eu customers. Telemetry shows ~20% of eu requests routed to fallback \"model-legacy\" while the canary should be 5% for pro tier. Anyone seen this?

Kevin: Hmm, did rollout scope include region? Our per-tier routing policy should evaluate region first then tier then canary. Can you paste config?

Maria: here's the config I used:
```
routing_policy:
  - match: {region: \"eu-*\", tier: \"pro\"}
    cohort: \"canary-v2\"
    weight: 0.05
  - match: {tier: \"pro\"}
    cohort: \"stable-v1\"
    weight: 0.95
fallback: \"model-legacy\"
```

Srinivas: This config looks fine at surface but there's a known matching bug where \"eu-*\" prefix doesn't match \"eu-west-2\" in our Matcher v1. Also runtime PR #412 changed fallback evaluation order (it now checks variant capability before cohort accounting).

Olivia: DevEx note — we shipped a kernel-compatibility guard that triggers fallback when the selected variant doesn't have a quantized kernel for a node type. That could explain why eu (older GPU pool) falls back.

Maria: Observing that fallback is 100% for requests >1024 tokens; under that threshold the canary behaves as expected. Suggests kernel selection failure for long sequences.

Kevin: Can we repro with a synthetic request and capture smart-router logs? Also we should add explicit tags to metrics: cohort_evaluation.reason

Maria: Repro payload:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD\" \
  -d '{\"model\":\"canary-v2\",\"input\": "x" * 1100, \"region\":\"eu-west-2\", \"tier\":\"pro\"}'
```

Srinivas: Reproduced locally. Logs show: \"variant_not_compatible: no_qkernel\" from kernel-resolver in smart-router. Flow is: matcher -> choose cohort -> attempt variant selection -> if variant incompatible, immediate fallback and DECREMENT canary exposure count. That's the problem.

Olivia: My take — fallback should be graceful but shouldn't consume canary exposure quota when selection fails due to environment (kernel/hw). Otherwise our canary metrics underreport failures and bias decisions.

ux-jamie: From rollout UX perspective, customers expect canary exposure stats to show attempted vs completed exposures + failure reasons. Console should surface \"attempted\", \"succeeded\", and \"fallback_reason\" breakdowns by tier/region.

Kevin: Agreed. Plan: (1) change smart-router to emit attempt tag and an outcome tag (attempted/success/failed_variant). (2) when variant selection fails, tag metric as attempted but increment a separate counter for failed_variant and route to fallback without decrementing canary quota. (3) update /v1/routing debug schema to include \"cohort_attempted\": true/false and \"fallback_reason\".

Maria: I'll open a hotfix PR for smart-router to add the tags + adjust quota decrement timing. Will also patch Matcher to fix region wildcard.

Srinivas: Also add unit test for long-seq kernel selection and integration test that validates canary exposure accounting.

Olivia: I'll add a Console dashboard panel: Canary exposures by tier/region with columns: attempted, success, fallback_reason. Will coordinate with Product for telemetry naming.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: smart-router/hotfix -> staging

Maria: Thanks — will post PR link in a bit. SRE: please watch eu latency & error budget for next hour.

Kevin: Pinging @oncall for visibility. :eyes:
